Twelve targets, three decision layers, and one with no controls

The last report asked which search method could fit twelve targets at once, and the answer arrived overnight: twelve of its twenty recommendations are already in the tree. This pass can therefore ask the next question, and it has a harder answer. Four of the twelve modes are decided by a router that cannot see a single one of the parameters declared to govern them — so the cheapest decisive experiment in the project is, as designed, undecidable on three of its four modes.

One paragraph

The verdict. The instrument is in better repair than at any point in its history and the model is no closer to its goal. In one day the objective was restated onto the goal's twelve modes, the search space grew from 5 movable fields to 21, crowding disutility reached scoring for the first time, the ASC contraction was implemented, 336 GiB came back, and the licence boundary was closed — and no arm ran, so the scoreboard is the same reading it was. What this pass adds is the reason that matters: the project's remaining deviations are not distributed across its parameters, they are concentrated in a layer that has no parameters. Fixing that is a mechanism change, not a calibration.

Section 1

Method

What was read, by whom, and what each number is allowed to mean.

Six agents worked one phase each, in parallel, over one commit: a code reviewer across six areas, a performance analyst, a historian, a document reviewer and two researchers. Three collector scripts produced every mechanical figure, so nothing in the tiles or the tables was typed. The writer took a seventh lane of its own — the measurements in Section 4, which are new to this pass — and then verified a sample: ten cited file:lines re-read by hand and four sources re-fetched.

Two rules govern every number here. A run is a result only when its _run.json says ran_to_last_iteration; no arm in this project has said that since 21 August, so every scoreboard figure below is a reading at a stated iteration and nothing more. And a measurement that would need a run to make is written "unmeasured — needs a probe arm", never estimated as though it had been made.

Section 2

Twelve targets, three layers, and the one that has no controls

The pass's central finding, and the answer to "what architectures reach equilibrium across this many variables".

A calibration is a map from controls to targets. Before choosing an algorithm you have to know the map exists. This model decides its twelve modes in three different layers, and the targets are spread across them very unevenly.

LayerWhat decides itTargets it setsControls it has
1 · Plan generationbuild_activity_chains.py and the four binder passesride's ceiling, freight, external trafficB.ride.*, B.external.*, B.freight.* — five of them in the movable 21
2 · Mode choiceSubtourModeChoice over [car, ride, pt, bike, walk, taxi]car, ride, walk, bike, taxi — and pt in aggregatethe ASCs: 3 frozen, 1 the reference, 1 inert by construction, 1 usable
3 · Route and submodeSwissRailRaptorbus · heavy_rail · light_rail · ferrynone — §9.158 measured that the raptor's cost carries no mode constant, no fare and no distance term
The finding

Layer 3 has four targets and zero controls. No search method — grid, SPSA, CMA-ES, Bayesian optimisation, history matching, or an ASC contraction — can move a target through a control that does not exist. Four of the seven modes past the stop bar live there, and they fail in opposite directions (heavy rail +247.2 %, light rail −47.2 %), which is the classic signature of a mechanism defect rather than four wrong constants.

The evidence, measured at this commit

RUN.mode_choice.modes is [car, ride, pt, bike, walk, taxi], so pt is one alternative. The run's own modestats.csv carries a single pt column; its 100.legs.csv.gz resolves that column into bus 18,034 / rail 6,404 / tram 381 / ferry 314. The submode is chosen downstream of mode choice, by the router.

So the only channel a scoring constant has is plan selection — an agent shifting toward a higher-scoring plan already in memory. A whole-file pass over the F31 arm's plan memory at iteration 100 (ITERS/it.100/100.plans.xml.gz, 154,347 persons) measures how wide that channel is:

Measured in plan memory at iteration 100CountShare
Persons holding 8 plans / 9 plans111,746 / 42,601memory is saturated for every agent (max_agent_plan_memory = 8)
Persons holding any pt leg at all17,61611.4 %
Persons whose plans differ in which pt submode they use9740.63 % of the population
Tram legs across all plans in memory3,8171.57 % of the 242,891 pt legs
Ferry legs across all plans in memory2,7151.12 %

A scoring constant can therefore reallocate between pt submodes for well under one per cent of the population. Raising C.asc.light_rail cannot move a trip from heavy rail to light rail, because essentially no agent holds both a rail plan and a tram plan to choose between. It can only make already-tram plans likelier against car, bike and walk.

Consequence

What this does to the decisive experiment. The ~15 h ASC contraction test is built, costed and unrun. Its four modes are bike, bus, light rail and ferry. Only bike sits on an alternative the mode-choice operator can switch to. For the other three, a null result — "|Δ| did not shrink" — would be equally consistent with taste, with mechanism, and with the control is not connected to the choice. The experiment cannot separate its own two hypotheses on three of its four modes. It is decisive for bike and, as designed, undecidable for bus, light rail and ferry.

The same failure, three times, at three distances from the decision

This is not a one-off. The recurring class in this repository is a control declared in the registry that does not reach the layer it is meant to govern — and the three live instances sit at three different distances:

The registry's discipline is what makes this visible at all: every one of these is declared, with units and a sweep, so the gap between "declared" and "reaching the model" is inspectable. check_hardcoding.py catches a value typed into a script. Nothing catches a value declared in the registry that arrives in the wrong layer.

Section 4

Requirement 8 gets a derived answer, for the first time

New in this pass, at zero machine cost, from an arm already on disk.

GOAL.md requirement 8 asks for convergence within 250 iterations. It has never been measured: no arm since family F4 on 21 August has passed iteration 100, because the gate watcher kills the JVM at the first gate and seven modes are past the stop bar. The project has therefore been reading a model that is still moving, which is exactly what §9.158 and §9.159 discovered the hard way.

But the trajectory of a moving model is itself data. Taking the F31 arm's own modestats.csv and scorestats.csv at iterations 40, 70 and 100 and fitting a three-point geometric (Aitken) extrapolation to each series gives, for the first time, an estimate of where each one settles.

The estimate

The system settles around iteration 200–210 — inside the 250 the goal asks for, and correctly sized by the approved 300-iteration arm. The run is plainly not relaxed at 100: its average plan score is still 24 % below its own asymptote and rising monotonically. This is an extrapolation from one arm, not a measurement, and the depth arm is precisely the experiment that tests it.

Three consequences that change the plan

  • ride is converged at −38.0 % and will not move. Its decay constant is 0.054 and its asymptote equals its iteration-100 value to five decimal places. No further iteration and no constant closes ride: its deficit is plan generation. The previous report argued this; it is now measured.
  • car — the only mode inside the band — is moving away from its target. +2.41 % relative still to come on modestats' basis, taking the board's +5.4 % toward roughly +8 %. Still inside, but the margin is spent. The one green cell on the board is the least safe one.
  • walk gets worse, not better. −5.95 % relative still to come, taking −11.1 % toward roughly −16 % — from "over 10 %" toward the stop bar, as the model converges.
On the numbers

Basis caveat, stated. modestats.csv counts unlinked legs over the whole population including truck and freight; the board counts resident linked trips. The relative directions and decay constants transfer between the two; the exact deviations do not, and are written above as "toward roughly", never as board readings.

The choice set closes at iteration 74 — everything after is re-selection

modeChoiceCoverage1x.txt records the fraction of agents who have ever used each mode. The first iteration at which each is within 1 % of its final value: walk 7 · car 8 · bike 11 · ride 12 · taxi 13 · pt 74. Motorbike and truck never move at all — 0.00236 and 0.04158, constant from iteration 0, confirming both are locked carves outside RUN.mode_choice.modes.

pt is the last choice set to close and it closes at only 24.58 % of agents: three quarters of the population has never held a public-transport plan. From iteration 74 the model is doing pure score-based re-selection inside a frozen choice set — which is the regime in which an ASC step is well behaved, and in which the extrapolation above is trustworthy.

Section 5

The project in its field

49 comparable projects, 12 platforms, 14 calibration methods — read from a standing library, with 39 searches spent only on what it could not answer.

What the empty rung does and does not mean

A qualification this pass added, and it is honest rather than flattering. A trip-based four-step model — WFTDM, Wasatch Front, Utah — does report that rung: six transit modes separately, verbatim "All mode shares were calibrated to within 5% of observed data" and "Total transit trips and boardings were calibrated to within 5% of observed data (trips 1.6%, boardings −0.8%)". It is excluded from the survey for having no agents, which is right — but it means the empty rung is partly a reporting convention among agent-based models, not purely a difficulty. Re-verified from the source this pass.

What the field says that bears directly on this project

  • This project's hardest rule is the profession's rule, verbatim. Mode-constant adjustment *"should be considered 'a last resort'"* (TF Resource, re-fetched this pass). DECISIONS.md §8.5's freeze is mainstream practice, for the same stated reason: constants stand for unmeasured comfort, reliability and safety, so they mask structural error.
  • There is no published acceptance bar for mode choice at all — *"There are no applicable criteria guidelines for checks of mode choice."* The 10 % band in GOAL.md is self-imposed. Sibling components do carry tolerances, which makes the silence on mode choice a deliberate one.
  • The coupling is acknowledged and unsolved — *"when calibration actions are taken to increase the nonmotorized mode shares, the transit shares may be affected further"*. Shares sum to one; moving one mode moves the rest. The field's answer is a weighted sum and a human in the loop.
  • Nobody publishes an evaluation count, and there is now a paper explaining why. *The Calibration Illusion in Traffic Microsimulation* (Hickert et al., 2026) argues automatic calibration is *"largely an illusion"* because *"a significant — and unquantified — amount of bespoke manual work is hidden behind these methods"*, and that joint calibration is not identifiable. The same paper finds a 10 % change in the simulation timestep *"could more than double"* the error — a model setting dominating a behavioural one. The direct analogue here is a teleported access leg.

Architectures built for many targets at once — there are two, and neither is used in transport

ArchitectureHow it handles many targetsCost evidenceApplicability here
History matching / NROYImplausibility I(x) = |z − E(f(x))| / √(Var(e)+Var(d)+Var(f(x))), computed independently per output, with model discrepancy Var(d) an explicit term; returns the set not yet ruled out.Unpublished on a transport ABM — the tutorial reports only "three waves" and no design size.The closest fit to twelve per-mode deviations. An empty NROY region is a formal verdict that the deficit is structural — a published test of exactly the taste-or-mechanism question.
Epsilon-constraint / multi-objectiveOptimise one objective, bound the rest as inequality constraints — the textbook way to write "every mode inside 10 %" as a constraint set rather than a sum.No evaluation count published for any multi-objective transport calibration.NSGA-II has been coupled to MATSim, but for network design, not calibration. Epsilon-constraint appears nowhere in transport model calibration.
The scalarisation (what everyone actually does)A weighted sum of normalised squared deviations, plus a human deciding when to stop.Universal; unreported.A weighted sum can always be improved by trading a good mode against a bad one, and cannot reach a non-convex Pareto region for any weights. This project moved off it on 8 September.
The staged agency protocolNot an algorithm but an ordering: calibrate each component in sequence, pass validated results forward, constants last.No numbered protocol, no gating criterion, no rule for "constant vs mechanism" beyond "exhaust the other causes first".Maps onto this model's three layers — and says the work is currently pointed at the wrong one.
The placing

Where this project is ahead of its field, and where it is behind. Ahead: CAL.objective.components is now goal_modes.max_abs_rel_pct — a maximum over twelve unfolded modes, not a mean over five folded categories. That is the minimax shape a feasibility goal requires, and on this survey's evidence no comparable project uses it. Also ahead: asc_fixed_point.py's contraction test — does |Δ| shrink between two damped rounds? — is a sharper and cheaper answer to "constant or mechanism" than anything the survey found, and it is this project's own invention. Behind: it has never run one, and Section 2 shows why three of its four modes cannot answer.

The top mover is the last cheap one on the board, and it is the third instance of Section 2's pattern. C.time_weights.beta_headway = 0.5 and beta_reliability = 1.3 are declared with literature sweeps, written into params/C1_parameters.json at build_params.py:99-100, and carry no matsim_param and no consumer — verified independently for this report. Bus at +54.6 % against light rail at −47.2 % is a service-quality inversion, and the two parameters that would price service quality reach a JSON file and stop there.

Every one of the 61 pull requests was authored, approved and merged by the same account.

The twelve-line history. 10 Aug (day 0): the root commit, then P1, P2 and P3 land as three pull requests in one day - a 2.3 GiB hashed data package, a 157,678-link MATSim network and a tour-based demand of 517,936 weekday agents. Nothing has run.

  • 11 Aug: P4 opens by pointing MATSim at P3's output; all thirty assembled sets refuse to load. Three defects, and the lesson that the checks asked whether artefacts were consistent, never whether a simulator could read them.
  • 11-16 Aug: a 73-commit branch declares every value in a registry, drives the hardcoding ledger to 0, and re-harvests OSM on a boundary-derived extent - the typed rectangle had clipped 87 of 1,500 core SA1s. Family F1 opens; the first arms run their full 1000 iterations.
  • 18-21 Aug: ride pairing is built and immediately measured to be starved (0.104 % of ride trips share an OD with a household car trip); escort binding moves pairability two orders of magnitude; walk, bike and ride become physically simulated. F4's two 1000-iteration arms produce the calibrated base - 10.65 pp MAE, infeasible - and are still the deepest runs in the project.
  • 20-21 Aug: process hardens after five of six stacked PRs fail to reach main. Direct commits are banned, one PR per session at /handoff. This is the last day any arm runs its declared horizon.
  • 24-27 Aug: the all-modes batch is built inert and then activated as one boundary (F6): explicit signals, tram priority, level crossings, native dwell, taxi. Every arm from here is stopped at a gate. Two document gates close the drift class that had left the front door three phases stale.
  • 28-29 Aug: twelve modes get twelve targets, and the first thing the new yardstick finds is a defect in itself - the PT composition counted another city's light rail stop, so heavy rail's apparent -1.5 % fit was an artefact. Four of that session's own conclusions are corrected in the same PR.
  • 30 Aug: the heaviest day in the project - 87 commits, eight family boundaries (F14 to F21), a demand the committed builder could no longer reproduce, and the document restructure that puts the goal on one page behind thirteen position pages.
  • 31 Aug - 2 Sep: the loop finally fires. F21 reads its iteration-100 gate with 0 of 12 modes inside; Opal fares are charged and F22 puts bus inside at +8.0 %, the first mode ever inside; income scaling then blunts the fare and F23 reads 0 of 12 again.
  • 3-7 Sep: the instrument turns on itself - five whole-repository reports in five days file and close 60-odd defects, the issue gate makes an open issue a launch blocker, destination choice is constrained at both ends, the holdout is caught informing the count targets, and car comes inside the band at the F28 gate for the first time. The 2-minute-iteration directive is answered with arithmetic: no.
  • 8 Sep, morning (day 29): F31's gate reads 1 of 12 inside (car +5.4 %), ride's mean trip length is within 6 % of observation while its share is -38 %, and a restored progress line reports that a third of all public-transport routing requests find no service at all.
  • 8 Sep, afternoon: the sixth assessment finds the calibration loop had never once executed - 5 movable fields of 482 against a four-number objective - and rebuilds it on the goal's twelve modes; a gate arm carries a _fit.json for the first time; then, 105 minutes later, the remedy that same record proposed for the reading point is built, measured WORSE than what it replaces, and retired on its own evidence, because the movement it would average away is a monotone trend. 336.4 GiB comes back to the store. No arm was launched in either session.

The correction chain

The historian traced 28 corrections across 21 pull requests — a later PR overturning an earlier one's stated conclusion. The chain deepens with age: input defects give way to yardstick defects and then to instrument defects. The three newest are the sharpest, and two of them landed since the previous report.

correctionwhat it overturnedelapsed
#138 / #152 / #158 → #166Five assessments had described a calibration loop converging slowly. There was no working loop at all — 5 movable fields of 482, the one mode constant belonging to taxi (the only mode with no independent target), an objective of four folded numbers against a twelve-mode goal, and an execute path that had never completed a single candidate.days
#166 → #166extract_metrics had failed on every arm since F4, so no gate-stopped arm could ever be read. aborted_20260908T100009_300it_25pct is the first gate arm in the project's history to carry a _fit.json.same PR
#166 → #168The windowed-reading remedy §9.158 proposed was built, measured over the same six arms and found worse than the point reading it replaced — heavy rail 41.46 deviation points against 24.88, four modes past the whole band instead of three — and retired on its own evidence, because every mode's series over iterations 40–100 is monotone without a reversal.105 minutes
#59 / #87 → #166EscortCoherenceListener created plans through the innovation-off tail, so every recorded relaxation verdict rested on a false premise. Requirement 8 was not merely unmeasured — it was unmeasurable.weeks
On the 105 minutes

That a session can build a remedy, measure it, find it worse than what it replaces and retire it within 105 minutes — writing the negative result into the permanent record and keeping the instrument so the finding survives — is the strongest process signal in this repository. It is also why the tiles above show an instrument improving while the scoreboard does not move.

Section 8

The documents, the process and the controls

Where the living documents disagree with each other, and which rules nothing enforces.

The layering holds and the reading budget holds: the handover contract's line counts measure 522–575 against their caps, the record's numbering is monotonic with 157 of 157 sections indexed, and all 25 archived files carry their frozen banner. What does not hold is agreement between the pages.

Twelve contradictions, and every one is on a position page

check_doc_currency.py pins live-state figures in README.md and STATUS.md to the artefacts that decide them, and it is green. The position pages are outside its reach, and they are where the drift now lives. Three of these were re-verified by hand for this report, and the sharpest are *self*-contradictions — one page carrying two states at once, because a session rewrote some of its bullets and left the rest.

Why this keeps happening

The pattern, and it is a process finding rather than eight separate defects. Position pages are defined as "the current truth per topic" and are being written as though they were append-only, so a page that a session partly rewrote now carries both states. The rule that would catch it — check_doc_currency.py's claim pinning — covers README.md and STATUS.md and one position page out of thirteen. Every contradiction above is in the twelve it does not cover.

The gate that passes because of the prose describing the gate

A vacuous pass on a launch gate

The board and PR #168 state: "The issue gate is GREEN unscoped for the first time — 20 open, every one awaiting a stated measurement, 0 blocking." Mechanically this is true and exactly reproducible: replaying issue_gate.evidence() over all 20 open issues, every one carries the label and returns a ≥ 40-character statement, so blocking() is empty.

Substantively it is false for three of them. Issues #49, #50 and #155 each carry an 8 September comment whose own first line is "This issue BLOCKS the launcher" and which says in terms that the issue states no measurement — #50 because "no mode × age cell exists in any dataset this project holds", #155 because what it waits on is 31 accept-or-declare decisions, #49 because "it is a standing product directive, not a run question". They pass because the gate's regex matches the sentence describing the gate — "requires an AWAITING-RUN: <measurement> line with real content" — capturing the literal placeholder as its evidence. A fourth, #167, passes on "AWAITING-RUN: nothing".

So the three issues the check was built for are the three it now waves through. The honest count is 20 open, 17 with a genuine stated measurement, 3 self-declaring none — and GOAL.md requirement 10 is not currently a gate.

What an iteration costs, and whether 250 is reachable

Every figure from a run's own <code>stopwatch.csv</code>. No arm has run since the previous report, so nothing on the model's clock is new.

Iteration, 25 %

An evaluation
7.66 h
to the iteration-100 gate — 3.1 a day, and they cannot be parallelised
250 iterations
18.5 h
band 18.4–26.5. 300 iterations: 22.2 h, band 22.0–31.7

The horizon is reachable in wall clock and has never once been reached in fact. No 25 % arm since F4 on 21 August has passed iteration 100; innovation_off_tail is null for every gate arm on disk. The approved depth_convergence_25pct arm, with its gate watcher disabled, is the first thing in this project ever allowed to get there.

Halving the iteration is priced out and the arithmetic is closed. The mobsim is 75.8 % of it and every lever inside is spent: 2.4× the qsim threads bought 5.6 % and 16 is saturated; the events pool is bracketed on both sides (1 saturated, 2 is +44.5 % slower, 4 and 12 equal), so its share is the price of not throttling the qsim rather than waste to recover; the time-variant network repair already took a plain iteration from 310 s to 205.5 s and cannot be spent twice. The two structural routes to 130 s are refused on settled grounds — FIFO link dynamics would hold every car behind a 1.25 m/s pedestrian, and teleporting walk or bike is what requirement 1 forbids and GenericRouteTeleporter now throws on. The one lever with a 2× in it is still the sample fraction, and it is still unmeasured on this stack.

On the price of the next arm

The 22.2 h quote is arithmetically sound and prices a stack that no longer exists. arm_cost.py's observed_arms() (:154) filters on fraction and profiled and on nothing else — it has no notion of a comparability family or of the class tree's digest. All five arms behind the band predate PtCrowdingScoring, the GenericRouteTeleporter per-mode counters, the NetworkDirectWalkPtRouter counter and the EscortCoherenceListener tail branch. It warns loudly about a stale run and says nothing about a stale build. Two error directions that do not cancel: the crowding scorer adds handlers on the two highest-volume event classes (~1.27 M extra dispatches an iteration) inside a pipeline already at its measured knee, while the innovation-off tail is worth roughly 14 minutes the flat model does not credit. The upward risk is larger and unquantified.

What the new bytecode costs is unmeasured, and the last two runs died at iteration 0

  • PtCrowdingScoring — two handlers on PersonEntersVehicleEvent and PersonLeavesVehicleEvent, a boxed Double per boarding and per alighting, and a sort plus *k* PersonScoreEvents in afterMobsim, a phase whose median is 0 s today. Correctly hoisted — the integral is per-vehicle, not per-passenger. Unmeasured.
  • GenericRouteTeleporter's per-mode counters — roughly 520 k String allocations and 520 k map operations an iteration, inside the mobsim. The one clearly hoistable item. Unmeasured.
  • NetworkDirectWalkPtRouter.REQUESTS — one contended CAS per PT routing request across 20 replanning threads, on code measured at 8.2 % of run CPU. Unmeasured.
  • Whether the HEAD stack runs at 25 % at all. The two most recent runs on disk, both 1 % smoke probes on 8 September, died at iteration 0 — one on TransitAgentTriesToTeleportException, one at PersonPrepareForSim.
The recommendation this pass would put first on cost

Spend half an hour before spending thirty-two. One 4-iteration unprofiled 25 % probe on HEAD bytecode is 2.3 % of the approved arm, and it is the only measurement that turns 22.2 h from a projection into a price. The project has its own recorded lesson here: at §9.153 the F30 arm ran 45 % over the price read from the arm before it, on a stack that differed by one line.

Build layer

src/build/ builds any city's layers from declared inputs; cities/<city>/build/ encodes this city's intervention, corridor and statistical geography. The session's structural change is OUTPUT_INPUTS, a module-level literal mapping each output glob to the inputs whose CONTENT reaches it, declared in 17 modules and read STATICALLY by build_manifest._script_declarations (:377-414), which ast.parses the producing script and literal_evals the assignment rather than executing it. ancestry() (:492) resolves per-output lineage with a four-valued scope (raw/output/script/none), so a row states whether its provenance was proven or merely bounded by the script's whole source - the first mechanism in the repository that distinguishes 'this file descends from OSM' from 'the script that wrote it also reads OSM'. build_timing.py is a per-builder wall-clock roll-up deliberately placed at cities/<city>/data/_build_timing.json, outside build_manifest.SCAN and inside .gitignore, so a wall time can never enter a hashed artefact.

Analysis and calibration

report_mode_ridership.py is the single reader of the twelve-mode board, and the session's design principle is that the objective, the gate and the board must be ONE number: fit.score_goal_modes (:107-190) does not re-derive deviations - it calls rmr.report() under redirect_stdout and reads rmr.LAST['rows'], taking the thresholds from rmr.GATE_PASS_PCT / GATE_STOP_PCT, which the reader resolves from CAL.gate.* at import (:80-82). calibrate.py then optimises goal_modes.max_abs_rel_pct - a MAXIMUM over TWELVE UNFOLDED modes in RELATIVE per cent - replacing mode_share.mean_abs_pp, a MEAN over FIVE FOLDED categories in PERCENTAGE POINTS. asc_fixed_point.py is a new, deliberately read-only instrument that inverts board deviations onto mode constants and refuses structurally at any held_fixed field, reusing calibrate.sweep_interval so the movability contract is decided in one place. The area's recurring weakness is module-level mutable globals used as return and parameter channels across module boundaries: report_mode_ridership.LAST (:76) and extract_metrics._READ_AT (:107).

Contract and checks

Three concentric rings. The SCHEMA ring (config/schema/) states what any city must supply; the REGISTRY ring (cities/<city>/registry/, 494 fields at HEAD) states this city's values with units, provenance and either a sweep, a held_fixed rule or a derived_from identity; the CHECK ring verifies the two agree and that nothing decided a value in a script. check_hardcoding.config_reach() (:840-900) is the strongest idea: it does not read code to decide whether a field reaches the model, it changes the value and watches the emitted config move, and its docstring (:845-847) says why. check_package.py's consumers check (:1626-1647) is the weaker text-based sibling - and it is the one that is red.

Acquisition and data

Fourteen jurisdiction-specific adapters, correctly quarantined inside cities/<city>/extract/ - where a place name and a jurisdiction's file format legitimately live. Raw downloads land under data/raw/ with a provenance_*.json; corrections happen here, never in the raw bytes. The session's only change to the area is the build_timing bootstrap appended to four adapters, which is correct for all four (overpass.py's __main__ block at :362-376 does real work after the timer starts).

MATSim extensions

Twelve config groups, nine event handlers/listeners, five engines and eighteen standalone probes, all bound in CitysimControler.assemble (a 528-line method) behind representation gates read from the config - ptCrowding.isInVehicleTime() at :597, incomeScoring.isEnabled() at :614 - so an extension a run does not declare is never installed. The house discipline for scoring extensions is stated once and followed: accumulate in the event handler, emit PersonScoreEvents in notifyAfterMobsim, because emitting from inside a handler re-enters the events manager mid-drain (PtCrowdingScoring.java:80-84, citing ParkingChargeHandler and BikeStressScoring). PtCrowdingScoring follows it exactly, sorts its emission by person id (:246-250), and keeps its integral PER VEHICLE rather than per passenger so an occupancy change is O(1) (:86-90). PtCrowdingConfigGroup uses an UNSET = -1.0 sentinel (:38-42) so a Java default cannot silently equal a registry value.

Why two of them did not land

The pattern worth naming. Two of the three items that did not land are the same shape: a fix that was verified against the half of the code it changed. The calibrator now sends --config-set and its new test greps the sending half; nothing checks that the receiving half records it, so the loop would die after paying a full arm's wall clock. The issue gate now demands an AWAITING-RUN: line with real content, and the check is satisfied by the prose describing the check. Both fixes are right; both tests look at the wrong end.

And what happened to the previous report's findings

The recommendations were taken up; the findings were not, and the gap between those two numbers is the most useful thing in this section. Of the previous report's code findings the reviewer re-checked 59 at this commit: 7 closed, 1 changed, and 51 still open unchanged. The document lane reports a similar shape — 7 closed, 6 changed, 7 still open, 5 new.

Every one of the seven closed defects is in src/calibrate/ — the loop's registry keys reaching the raw MATSim --set, the rebuild-stage misclassification, the run_inputs candidate that ran the shipped value. The session fixed the thing it set out to fix and touched almost nothing else, which is the right way to spend a day but leaves 51 known defects and risks standing in the areas it did not visit.

What did not change: the scoreboard. No arm ran. The reading is the same F31 iteration-100 gate it was, 1 of 12 modes inside the band. That is the whole shape of this pass — an instrument substantially repaired, a model that has not moved, and no measurement of the repair because nothing has executed the repaired stack.

Section 14

What to do next, ranked

By what it would prevent or move, over what it costs. The first three are a sequence, not a menu.

The order

The critical path is four steps and only one of them costs machine time. Correct the overlay description (minutes) → probe the new bytecode (0.5 h) → launch the depth arm (22–32 h) → then, and only then, read anything. Everything else in this list waits on step three, because calibrate.py --execute refuses while the reading drifts further than the band it is meant to resolve, and that drift is a convergence problem that only depth can settle.

What not to do, and the survey supports each refusal

  • Do not adopt SPSA, CMA-ES or plain Bayesian optimisation. Their published evaluation counts run to hundreds or thousands of full simulations, against a budget of about three evaluations a day that cannot be parallelised.
  • Do not adopt Cadyts as a calibration device. It is per-plan compensating offsets — exactly what §8.5 and .claude/CLAUDE.md forbid. It remains the strongest available *diagnostic*: the size of the offset it needs per station measures how much demand the model is missing, and where.
  • Do not fit any constant to a public-transport mode until layer 3 has a control. On this pass's measurement such a fit would be absorbing a router defect into a taste parameter, which is precisely the failure §8.5 exists to prevent — and the profession's own guidance calls constant adjustment "a last resort".
  • Do not rebuild the windowed reading. §9.159 measured it worse than the point reading and the cause retires it: the movement is a monotone trend, and a mean over a monotone series is its centre.

The rubric

Findings are defect (wrong today, with a failure scenario), risk (not wrong yet, and would be under a stated change) or smell (works, and costs to keep). Factor statuses are IN (wired and reaching the model), PARTIAL, ASC (folded into a mode constant), INERT (declared in the registry, read by nothing) and OUT. Ratings run 1–5 per area and are never averaged across areas.

How to reproduce this report

python .claude/skills/project-report/scripts/collect_metrics.py <dir>, then collect_code_metrics.py and collect_performance.py into the same directory; then the six phases of .claude/skills/project-report/SKILL.md. The two research lanes read docs/reports/reference/ first and search only its gaps — this pass spent 39 of 40 calls on the field lane over 8 rounds and 13 of 40 on the factor lane over 3, and re-searched not one stored row. The reference library is committed; the dated reports are prunable.

The measurements in Section 4 are reproducible from artefacts already on disk: results/raw/aborted_20260908T100009_300it_25pct/output/modestats.csv, scorestats.csv, modeChoiceCoverage1x.txt and ITERS/it.100/100.plans.xml.gz. The plan-memory pass streams the gzip and builds no XML tree; it took under two minutes over 154,347 persons.
